issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction exists
issues.why: The court must confirm it has statutory authority to hear a divorce action regardless of venue disputes.

issues.label: Personal jurisdiction over Robert
issues.why: Because dismissal was sought under Civ.R. 12(B)(2), the court must determine whether it can exercise personal jurisdiction over Robert.

issues.label: Service of process validity
issues.why: Whether and when service was perfected affects jurisdictional-priority and potentially personal jurisdiction.

issues.label: Venue in Franklin County
issues.why: The court must decide if Franklin County satisfies any Civ.R. 3(C) venue basis pleaded (e.g., where claim arose, defendant residence/business) including (9).

issues.label: Venue in Perry County
issues.why: The proper forum for the case depends on whether Perry County is a proper venue under Civ.R. 3(C), especially 3(C)(9).

issues.label: Meaning of Civ.R. 3(C)(9)
issues.why: The court must interpret the divorce-specific venue provision, including what “resided for 90 days” requires.

issues.label: Is 3(C)(9) exclusive
issues.why: The court must decide whether Civ.R. 3(C)(9) displaces other Civ.R. 3(C) bases in divorce cases or merely provides an additional option.

issues.label: Residency vs domicile standard
issues.why: Applying 3(C)(9) requires defining “resided” (physical presence, intent, domicile) and how temporary absence/move affects it.

issues.label: Ninety-day lookback date
issues.why: The court must decide whether the 90-day period is measured from Wendee’s filing date, Robert’s filing date, or each complaint’s filing date separately.

issues.label: County of residence fact findings
issues.why: The court must determine where each party actually lived during the relevant 90-day period (Franklin vs Perry) based on evidence.

issues.label: Alternative venue bases alleged
issues.why: The Franklin complaint alleged claim arose and Robert’s business in Franklin County, requiring legal/factual findings if those bases remain available.

issues.label: Where claim for relief arose
issues.why: If not limited to 3(C)(9), the court must determine where the divorce claim “arose” for venue under Civ.R. 3(C)(1)/(2) concepts as pleaded.

issues.label: Principal place of business relevance
issues.why: The court must decide whether Robert’s principal place of business supports venue in a domestic relations divorce action under Civ.R. 3(C).

issues.label: Jurisdictional-priority rule applicability
issues.why: With two courts and two divorce complaints, the court must decide whether the first-filed/first-served court has priority to proceed.

issues.label: Priority prerequisites met
issues.why: Priority depends on both courts having concurrent jurisdiction and on first filing plus perfected service in the earlier case.

issues.label: Effect of improper venue on priority
issues.why: The court must resolve whether an improperly venued first action defeats jurisdictional priority or whether priority still attaches absent lack of jurisdiction.

issues.label: Distinguish venue from jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must avoid treating venue defects as jurisdictional defects when ruling under Civ.R. 12(B)(2) vs 12(B)(3).

issues.label: Proper remedy for improper venue
issues.why: The court must determine whether dismissal is appropriate or whether transfer/change of venue is required/available under Ohio procedure.

issues.label: Dismissal with or without prejudice
issues.why: If dismissal is ordered, the court must specify its preclusive effect and ensure it does not improperly adjudicate merits.

issues.label: Authority to direct other court
issues.why: The Franklin court must determine whether it can order the parties to proceed in Perry County or whether comity/priority limits such directives.

issues.label: Preclusion/comity between courts
issues.why: Competing rulings (Perry denying dismissal; Franklin dismissing) raise whether one court’s interlocutory venue ruling affects the other.

issues.label: Impact of Perry denial order
issues.why: The court must consider whether the Perry court’s May 23 order has any binding effect (law of the case, collateral estoppel) or is merely persuasive.

issues.label: Effect of Perry inactive docket
issues.why: The procedural status of the Perry case may affect mootness, timing, and practical ability to proceed but not necessarily jurisdiction.

issues.label: Waiver of venue objection
issues.why: The court must decide whether Robert timely asserted improper venue in Franklin County or waived it by appearance/filings.

issues.label: Waiver of personal jurisdiction defense
issues.why: If Robert sought relief inconsistent with lack of personal jurisdiction, the court must decide if Civ.R. 12(B)(2) was preserved or waived.

issues.label: Timeliness of Civ.R. 12 defenses
issues.why: The court must ensure Civ.R. 12(B)(2)/(3) defenses were raised in the first responsive pleading or by proper motion.

issues.label: Standard for Civ.R. 12(B)(3)
issues.why: The court must decide the evidentiary burden and whether to resolve disputed facts on venue via hearing, affidavits, or pleadings.

issues.label: Standard for Civ.R. 12(B)(2)
issues.why: The court must apply the correct burden-shifting and evidence standard for personal jurisdiction challenges.

issues.label: Need for evidentiary hearing
issues.why: If residency/venue facts are disputed, the court must decide whether due process requires an evidentiary hearing beyond oral argument.

issues.label: Domestic relations local rules
issues.why: Local domestic relations venue/jurisdiction rules may supplement Civ.R. 3(C)(9) and must be considered if applicable.

issues.label: Statutory residency for divorce
issues.why: Separate from venue, Ohio statutes impose state residency requirements for divorce; the court must ensure they are met.

issues.label: Forum shopping concerns
issues.why: Competing filings may invite equitable considerations, but the court must decide what role (if any) fairness plays in applying Civ.R. 3(C)(9)/priority.

issues.label: Equitable discretion scope
issues.why: The trial court’s stated fairness rationale requires deciding whether discretion exists to choose among forums when rules otherwise control.

issues.label: Abuse-of-discretion vs de novo review
issues.why: To decide correctly and create a proper record, the court must identify which issues are legal (de novo) versus factual/discretionary.

issues.label: Proper record and findings
issues.why: The court must make sufficient findings on residency, venue bases, and priority to permit meaningful appellate review.

issues.label: Effect of certified mail/process server
issues.why: Priority and jurisdiction may depend on the exact method, date, and completion of service in Franklin County.

issues.label: Concurrent proceedings management
issues.why: The court must address whether to stay rather than dismiss to avoid inconsistent judgments and preserve priority considerations.

issues.label: Mootness/ripeness of priority dispute
issues.why: Given dismissals/stays/inactive docket, the court must ensure the controversy over which court proceeds remains justiciable.

issues.label: Relief consistent with Civ.R. 3
issues.why: Any ruling must align with the procedural rules governing venue determination and the consequences of improper venue.
